newsitem.title: CHINA: Jailed U.S. businessman appeals Chinese jail term.
newsitem.headline: Jailed U.S. businessman appeals Chinese jail term.

text.p: A U.S. businessman jailed for 10 years in Shanghai this week for illegally importing garbage into China has appealed the sentence, a U.S. consular official said on Friday.

Shanghai-born William Ping Chen, now a resident of Oakland, California, was sentenced by a Shanghai court on Monday to 10 years in jail, deportation and ordered to pay a 500,000 yuan ($60,000) fine after he confessed to smuggling 238 tonnes of garbage and medical waste into the city in 1995.
The consular official said the consulate had been informed that Chen, 56, had appealed the sentence but said he had no further information.
Chen's lawyer, Yuan Jiyu, said his client had not filed any appeal through him.
"But I don't rule out the possibility that he used another lawyer or spoke to the court officials directly," he said.

Chen was arrested in June last year and sentenced after an open hearing on December 2 attended by an official from the U.S. consulate in Shanghai. The official Xinhua news agency said he pleaded guilty to the charges.

Chen's arrest was the climax of an emotional campaign launched by China in mid-1996 over illegal shipments of U.S. garbage listed as waste paper for recycling but found to contain old clothes, rubber gloves, and disposable syringes.

Chen had listed the imports as waste paper and mixed paper, and proceeded with the shipments despite warnings from Shanghai environmental officials and opposition from his Chinese joint venture partners, Xinhua said.
